findings.body: The real producer emits a running worker with `started_at: null` when its start was not recorded (`src/forge/board.py:249–250`), and the existing command test explicitly verifies that output (`tests/test_machine_views.py:281`). This validator rejects that legitimate row, causing the entire refresh to fail and leaving every story, check and finding absent or stale. Allow a null start time in the worker type and validator, and render its elapsed time as unknown.
findings.title: Accept unknown worker start times from the board contract

findings.body: The shared formatter omits required information that CORE owns. It always prints agent/test counts even without lane data, where detail 2 requires the next command alone, and prints `next.line` without exposing an available `next.command`. At line 27, a completed stage with `seconds` also loses its outcome: failed and successful Tests stages both become `Tests 5s`. These omissions affect the headless `/forge` reply already shipped here, independently of the pane and strip rendering deferred by the coordinator. Preserve stage outcomes and format the next command and no-lanes state as specified; cover those outputs through `/forge`.
findings.title: Not done: /forge returns the summary of detail 2

findings.body: The elapsed-time assertion occurs after advancing exactly 10 seconds, which also runs the next scheduled refresh. It therefore passes if `/forge` incorrectly computes elapsed time from `data.refreshedAt` instead of the current clock. The packaged tests do not assert worker elapsed time either. Add the required entry-point check before the next tick—for example, advance five seconds, verify that no refresh ran, and assert that `/forge` reports five additional seconds.
findings.title: Not done: elapsed time advances between refreshes
